title: Performance Markers and the User Timing API
description: Learn how to use the User Timing API, PerformanceObserver, and custom marks to measure and instrument real user interactions.

data.text: The User Timing API lets developers place markers and measures in their code to instrument real user flows. These markers appear in the DevTools Performance panel and can be aggregated to understand exactly where time is spent in complex interactions.

performance.mark() records a named timestamp. performance.measure() computes the duration between two marks or between a mark and the navigation start. Use them to measure loading, rendering, and interaction milestones.

data.title: User Timing API Examples
data.content: Instrument a checkout flow with marks and measures.

data.text: The PerformanceObserver API lets you observe entries as they are recorded. Use it to watch for long tasks, largest contentful paints, layout shifts, and custom marks in real time without polling.

data.title: PerformanceObserver for Long Tasks and LCP
data.content: Observe runtime performance events as they happen.

data.text: The Navigation Timing API provides high-resolution timestamps for every stage of page load. The Resource Timing API does the same for individual assets. Together they let you measure exactly where load time is spent: DNS, TCP, request, response, or DOM processing.

data.title: Navigation Timing Breakdown

data.text: Place marks around key user flows in React: clicks, form submissions, and navigation transitions. Measure from interaction start to paint to quantify perceived latency.

data.content: Measure interaction latency in a React component.

data.title: Clear Marks in Production
data.text: The performance buffer has a finite size. In production, periodically clear marks and measures, or rely on PerformanceObserver to consume entries as they arrive. Never leave thousands of unobserved entries in memory.

terms.definition: A named timestamp recorded with performance.mark() for later measurement.
A duration calculated between two marks or between a mark and navigation start.
An API for asynchronously observing performance entries as they are recorded.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use performance.mark() and performance.measure() to instrument real user flows
PerformanceObserver lets you watch entries in real time
Navigation Timing gives per-stage page-load breakdowns
Resource Timing shows asset-level download and latency details
Clear marks periodically to avoid exhausting the performance buffer
Pair custom marks with field metrics to connect lab and production
data.takeaway: Custom performance markers turn vague intuition into hard numbers. Instrument the interactions that matter most, observe them in production, and use the data to prioritize optimization work.
